annotation_target.structure: A strophic ballad built over a single repeating accompaniment cell. The eleven-measure group (10, 14, 18, 34, 42, 62, 66, 70, 86, 90, 98) and an even larger near-identical group of thirteen measures sharing the same figure show this G-rooted pattern recurring roughly every 4 measures within each verse and then again across every subsequent verse. Density stays gentle and even throughout — among the busiest measures are 7, 23, 31, 47, and 55 (all 11 onsets), spread evenly across the form rather than clustering at a climax, matching the song's plain, walking-tempo accompaniment.

teaching_goals: Repeating accompaniment vamp technique: practice the G-rooted figure that recurs at measures 10, 14, 18, 34, 42, 62, 66, 70, 86, 90, and 98 until it's completely automatic — chord-window analysis shows G major and D/D7 (a I-V vamp, not I-IV-V) covering the great majority of this 105-measure piece, with no C or F chord detected anywhere.
Long-form strophic awareness: learn to recognize where the accompaniment cell restarts for each new verse so you can keep your place across a piece this long without losing count.
Even, walking-tempo phrasing: with density spread gently and evenly (no measure exceeding 11 onsets), practice a steady, unhurried 2/4 pulse rather than reaching for dynamic drama.
Solo ballad range: use the right hand's comfortably singable octave-plus range to practice supporting a vocal line without ever overpowering it.
style_tips: Once the recurring G-rooted accompaniment figure is secure, let your attention go entirely to the melody and its long, singing phrases — the accompaniment should feel automatic, not effortful.
Keep the 2/4 tempo walking and unhurried — this is a ballad about longing and distance, not urgency.
